name: inprocess-ahb-cvw-apb-timer-dma-refusal-f1f4
notes: One AHB-Lite CPU (CORE-V Wally / CVW) as the single manager of its external bus, and one PULP APB3 timer target behind the generated ahb_lite_memory_target beat adapter; no DMA model is declared, so F6 is refused by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB)

CVW bakes RESET_VECTOR = 0xC0000000 into its derived configuration and its external-memory window is 0xC0000000..0xCFFFFFFF, so both the RAM image and the APB target window must live inside that range or HSELEXT is never asserted for them: RAM is 0xC0000000+64 KiB and the target window is the timer profile's declared 4 KiB window at 0xC8000000
F1 is refused by name (unsupported-f1:no-retirement-observation:ahb_cvw): the AHB boundary exports no RVFI/commit channel, and a fetch beat is not a retirement
F5 is refused by name (unsupported-f5:cpu-irq-unexported:ahb_cvw): the AHB boundary exports no interrupt input at all, so the timer's own declared F5 facts have nowhere to be delivered
the cpu and target declare 50 MHz, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives both models
the CPU keeps its instruction cache: F2-F4 change only RAM/mailbox data, so the trampoline slot and the firmware code are fixed after boot and no cache invalidation is claimed

The expected refusal is "unsupported-f6:cpu-dma-port-unexported:ahb:the-ahb-boundary-has-no-dma-port": the flow is named, not silently dropped, and nothing is claimed about a DMA that was never built.
description: One AHB-Lite CVW CPU and one PULP APB3 timer, plus a declared ZipDMA profile. The AHB-Lite boundary has no DMA port in the unified entry, so the CPU/DMA combination refuses F6 by name at declaration time; the refusal is the evidence, and no bus access is reported as an F6 transfer.
